summary: The test script is syntactically correct and uses Playwright APIs properly with awaited assertions on locators. However, the selectors rely heavily on guessed data-test attributes without validation evidence, which reduces selector robustness. The test case lacks any parameterization or reuse abstractions, causing a lengthy and repetitive script which impacts maintainability and reusability. No testCaseId preservation in the test title is present. There is no negative or edge case coverage, and the URL is hardcoded without config usage.

issues.description: Selectors use hardcoded data-test attributes which may be guessed without verification of their existence or stability.
issues.recommendation: Verify selectors against the UI or use more robust selector strategies or centralized selector definitions.

issues.description: Test case title does not preserve the original testCaseId (TC-001) from the generation mapping.
issues.recommendation: Include testCaseId in test titles for traceability and easier mapping back to test cases.

issues.description: The script contains many repetitive lines checking visibility of product cards individually which reduces maintainability.
issues.recommendation: Use loops or array-driven testing to iterate product selectors, improving code brevity and maintainability.

issues.description: The URL is hardcoded directly inside the test.
issues.recommendation: Consider using environment configurations or a baseURL to support different environments and improve flexibility.

recommendations: Add testCaseId to test titles for direct traceability.
Refactor the test to iterate over product IDs using loops or test.each style for reusability.
Validate selectors against the actual application to ensure they target stable attributes.
Externalize the base URL to a configuration file or environment variable.
Expand assertions to not only check visibility but also content or functionality if applicable.
